items.stem: You insert user-supplied data into a database. Which PHP approach best prevents SQL injection?

options.text: A PDO prepared statement with bound parameters
options.rationale: Correct: prepared statements send data separately from SQL, so input cannot alter the query.
That escapes HTML output, not SQL input.

options.text: Concatenating the value into the query string
options.rationale: Concatenation is exactly what enables injection.
Hiding errors does nothing for injection risk.

items.stem: Which comparison in PHP checks both value and type with no type juggling?

options.rationale: Correct: the identity operator compares value and type without coercion.
The loose operator performs type juggling and can give surprising results.
A single equals sign is assignment, not comparison.
That is a loose inequality operator and still juggles types.

items.stem: Which TWO practices reduce cross-site scripting (XSS) risk when rendering user content in PHP? (Select TWO)

options.text: Escaping output with htmlspecialchars() before echoing
options.rationale: Correct: escaping neutralises HTML metacharacters in output.

options.text: Validating and constraining input on the server
options.rationale: Correct: server-side validation limits what untrusted data can contain.

options.text: Storing the raw input unchanged and echoing it later
options.rationale: Echoing raw input is the XSS vulnerability itself.
That does not affect how the page renders injected markup.

items.explanation: Correct: escaping neutralises HTML metacharacters in output.; Correct: server-side validation limits what untrusted data can contain.
